Apple has updated the privacy policy of its Apple Store app, adding provisions related to a not-yet-launched virtual shopping assistant. Details below.

Apple is expanding the use of artificial intelligence in its retail business

As discovered by MacRumors, the Apple Store app and its privacy page have now added a new section titled "Virtual Shopping Assistant," which reads as follows:

In other words, the Apple Store app may soon feature a chatbot that uses user data to provide personalised responses, helping users make purchasing decisions.

Apple says it will strip personally identifiable information from conversations before sharing them with unnamed partners to power assistant responses — a practice that likely suggests third-party models will be supporting parts of the experience.

Conversation history will be kept within the app for users to revisit, and will also be retained for Apple's business analytics. Users can independently choose, via a new "Chat Improvements" setting, whether to allow their conversations to be used to improve the virtual shopping assistant.

The wording of Apple's privacy policy suggests the virtual assistant may initially roll out in only select countries and regions, and could debut first in English-speaking markets before expanding to other languages and territories.

Several months before this news, Apple had already introduced an AI chatbot within its internal Sales Coach app, providing sales and technical resources for the company's retail partners. Accessible via the "Ask" tab, the chatbot answers questions based on official Apple training materials and documentation.

Previously, Bloomberg also reported that Apple is testing a system called "Live Notes" at some retail stores, which uses AI to record, transcribe and summarise Genius Bar service sessions, allowing employees to focus on assisting customers rather than taking notes.

To learn more about the Apple Store app and its privacy practices, click here.

What do you think — would a chatbot in the Apple Store app actually be useful? Share your thoughts in the comments.
